text:
Dylan: Heads up — product wants a canary that targets 5% of traffic for the new safety-filter model, but only for requests with X-Client-Beta: true header. Also needs to count against the same quota bucket as the primary model. How do we wire header-matching + sticky sessions + per-route quota?
Priya: We can do header-first routing, then weight split. For sticky sessions we should prefer a session cookie or X-Session-Id consistent-hash so users see the same variant. Quota-wise, route should reference the same quota key (e.g., quota_key: model-primary).
Jin: Agree. Important: ensure the canary sampling happens after auth so quota attribution uses authenticated identity (sub/email). Otherwise we split anonymous traffic incorrectly. Also add telemetry tags so we can slice metrics by canary=true.
Ava: UX ask — console should show an estimated qps delta for the canary and a preview of which headers will match. Ops wants an easy rollback button that flips weight to 0. Could we show a small histogram of sampled latency for the canary vs baseline in the rollout panel?
Dylan: Good call on auth-first. For sticky: do we rely on cookie->consistent-hash -> route, or header-based sticky? Some clients set headers inconsistently.
Priya: Prefer session-id hash. Sample policy: first check X-Client-Beta header; if present route to splitter with weights {canary:5, baseline:95}. If no header, route to baseline. Pseudoconfig: 
```yaml
- match:
    headers:
      X-Client-Beta: "true"
  route:
    splitter:
      key: "session_id"   # uses X-Session-Id or cookie fallback
      variants:
        - id: canary-model
          weight: 5
        - id: baseline
          weight: 95
      quota_ref: "model-primary-quota"
      telemetry_tags:
        - canary_id: "safety-filter-v2"
        - sampled: "true"
```
Jin: Additions: 1) If session_id missing, fall back to consistent_hash(client_ip + user_agent) but mark telemetry: "fallback_shard":"ip_ua". 2) Emit a 'route_bucket' tag (canary/baseline) and expose it in the console metrics.
Ava: For console rollout controls: editable weight slider, a forced-override toggle (apply to 100% of a specific user/email for QA), and quick telemetry sparklines (latency, error rate, token cost). Can we also surface the quota burn rate for the referenced quota in the same panel?
Dylan: Yes. Concern: quota_ref pointing to same quota implies canary could cause spike and starve baseline. Maybe we should allow "quota_shares" where canary and baseline consume the same quota but with reservation or soft limits. Thoughts?
Priya: Two options: 1) shared quota (simple) — both decrement same bucket. 2) reservation policy — allocate X% of quota to canary for protected experiments. For small 5% experiments, reservation isn't necessary unless you're near limits. We should implement both, default to shared with an optional reservation field.
Jin: Telemetry plan: add a durable counter metric 'route.canary.safety-filter-v2.requests' plus a histogram 'route.canary.safety-filter-v2.latency'. Tag each metric with customer_id, route_bucket, quota_key. That lets alerts be written against canary-only latencies.
deploy-bot: canary rollout created by @Priya — split safety-filter-v2 5% weight on header X-Client-Beta:true, quota_ref=model-primary-quota. See: https://console.redwood.tools/rollouts/rl-8432
Ava: One more UX nit — show a small sample of live requests that matched the canary (sanitized) so engineers can validate inputs quickly (no PII).
Dylan: OK next steps: Priya to prototype route YAML + fallback hashing, Jin to add telemetry counters and tags, Ava to mock console panel with weight slider + quota burn preview. I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow. :+1:
